grammar.title: 8B: Reported speech - sentences and questions
grammar.explanation:
We use **reported speech** when we tell a **relative** what someone said. We report the idea, not the exact words.

When the verb is past, like **said** or **told**, the tense moves back one step. "I am **engaged**" becomes **he said he was engaged**.

**will** becomes **would** and **can** becomes **could**. "I will **babysit**" becomes **she said she would babysit**.

Use **say** with no person and **tell** with a person. "I love the **wedding** photos" becomes: she **said** she loved the wedding photos. She **told me** she loved the wedding photos. The word **that** is optional.

Time and place words change too. "Tomorrow" becomes **the next day** and "here" becomes **there**. "We **argue** here" becomes **they said they argued there**.

For reported questions, use **asked** and normal word order. Do not use **do** or **did**. "Where did you **raise** your kids?" becomes **she asked me where I raised** my kids.

For yes/no questions, add **if** or **whether**. "Will you **forgive** me?" becomes **she asked if I would forgive** her.
examples: *Tom *told me* he would plan the wedding.* (tell + person)
*He *said* he *would* babysit on Friday.* (will becomes would)
*They *asked* where we *lived*.* (question word order, no do/did)
*My relative *said* they *had* visited us the *day before*.* (time shift)
